stem.text: The function f is differentiable for all real numbers, and selected values of f are given in the table. Must there be a value c, with \( 0 < c < 7 \), for which \( f(c) = -2 \)? Justify your answer.

answer_key.label: Yes. Since f is differentiable, it is continuous on \( [0, 7] \), and \( f(0) = -9 < -2 < f(7) = 5 \), so the Intermediate Value Theorem gives at least one such c.

worked_solution.text: Because f is differentiable, f is continuous, in particular on \( [0, 7] \).
From the table, \( f(0) = -9 < -2 < f(7) = 5 \), so -2 lies between the values of f at the ends of \( [0, 7] \).
By the Intermediate Value Theorem there is at least one c with \( 0 < c < 7 \) and \( f(c) = -2 \). So yes, such a c must exist.
